## 373 · Opening a pull request through the session's GitHub tool added a link to the chat, and an edit does not take it out of the history

**Enforced by:** CHECKLIST pr-body-read-back — after creating a pull request, read its description back at once and remove any footer that links to a chat session. Then tell the owner that the first revision stays in the description's edit history, where only the owner can delete it.

**Smell:** a pull request description ending in a rule and a "Generated by" line that the text sent did not contain.

**Recorded 2026-09-29.** A promotion pull request was created in a public repository with a body carrying no trailer, as Doctrine §9b requires. Read back, the stored body ended in a footer the server had added: a rule, then an attribution line whose link was the chat session. The body was corrected within a minute, and the corrected text carries no link.

GitHub keeps every revision of a description, and the first one, with the link, is still listed in its edit history. None of this family's privacy gates can see it: `privacy-check.mjs` reads the tree, `privacy-history-check.mjs` reads commits and commit messages, and a pull request description is neither.

**What only the owner can do.** On the pull request, the "edited" menu on the description lists its revisions, and deleting the first removes the link. The session's GitHub tools read and update a body and cannot delete a revision.

**What would close it.** A gate that reads pull request descriptions, and their edit histories, for the SESSION_LINKS class in `privacy-patterns.mjs`. It is not built. Until it is, the read-back above is the only thing between the tool's footer and a public page.
